content:
- Applied improve-code-boundaries smell-10 in src/process/session.rs by inlining DesiredManagedPostgresSession -> ManagedPostgresStartIntent conversion into ManagedPostgresSessionMaterializer::materialize and deleting the one-caller helper.
- Validation: make check passed, make lint passed, focused cargo nextest run on process::session tests passed; make test failed twice on the already-tracked incremental-linking bug while building tests/ha.rs with missing rcgu object files.
- Committed and pushed 6783acb (Inline managed session start intent), then ran bash .ralph/task_switch.sh; it succeeded but again printed the known rm error for missing .ralph/current_task.txt.

- Read prior Ralph progress for this agent; there was no visible prior content returned.
- Loaded improve-code-boundaries skill instructions and confirmed I must inspect found_smells first.
- Checked git status and repo file inventory; only .ralph bookkeeping is already dirty so far.
- Next: inspect found_smells, choose one boundary smell, then refactor and validate with lint/tests.

- Confirmed there are no queued found_smells beyond .gitkeep, so I am selecting a fresh boundary smell.
- Read smell-10 and smell-1 guidance; I’m prioritizing wrapper/one-caller helper removal with proof from the compiler/call graph.
- Next: inspect startup/state modules and helper-heavy spots for one concrete overabstraction to flatten.

- HA startup/state no longer had the old wrapper smell; I skipped it rather than reworking already-flat code.
- API worker and a few other modules still show private helper layering, type aliases, and startup/request glue worth checking.
- Next: prove helper call counts and pick the narrowest flattening that deletes fake boundaries instead of shuffling code.

- The cleanest live smell so far is duplicate `PgConnInfo` projection in CLI connection rendering rather than already-flattened HA startup code.
- I confirmed the repo has a canonical `PgConnInfo` type but no obvious shared constructor for the repeated “postgres/postgres + target endpoint + TLS” shape.
- Next: inspect other construction sites to see whether a constructor on the canonical type can remove duplicate field wiring across modules, not just inside one function.

- Flattened the API startup boundary: removed `ApiRuntimeRequest`, `ApiRuntime`, and `ApiWorker`, and made startup return the real `ApiRuntimeCtx`.
- Updated the runtime worker join path and dev-support router builder to call the simplified startup and use `worker::run` / `startup::into_router` directly.
- Next: clear any stale references, then run lint and full test targets required by the task.

- Compile fallout from the wrapper deletion was limited to `worker::run` visibility; I fixed that by adding `startup::run(ctx)` instead of reintroducing a wrapper type.
- The remaining diff is a real reduction: API startup now exposes `bootstrap`, `run`, and `into_router` over the actual `ApiRuntimeCtx`.
- Next: finish compile validation, then run `make lint` and `make test` as required before committing.

- Finished the API startup boundary refactor and confirmed it passes `cargo check`.
- Starting required repo validation with `make lint`, followed by `make test` if lint is clean.
- Next: fix any lint/test failures, then commit/push and switch the Ralph task.

- `make lint` passed cleanly after the API startup boundary simplification.
- Starting `make test` now; I will fix any regression before committing.
- Next: complete tests, then commit the source and .ralph updates, push, and run task switch.

- `make test` is still running under `cargo nextest`; current code delta is net-negative, mostly from deleting API wrapper types.
- No new smells or hidden failures surfaced yet beyond the earlier visibility fix.
- Next: wait for test completion, then either fix fallout or finish git/ralph handoff.

- `make test` is deep into the `nextest` run and currently green from the visible output.
- The suite reported a few existing `LEAK` markers in API worker tests but kept running; nothing points to a regression from this boundary cleanup.
- Next: capture the final test exit, then commit/push and hand off with task switch.

- Validation completed: `make lint` passed and `make test` passed (237 tests, 5 known leaky tests already tracked in backlog).
- Confirmed the leaky test issue already has existing bug files, so no duplicate bug task was created.
- Next: stage source + .ralph bookkeeping, commit, push, and run `.ralph/task_switch.sh`.

- Staged the source and Ralph bookkeeping changes and started the git commit.
- The commit hook is currently running docs publication/lint as part of commit validation.
- Next: wait for commit completion, then push `master` and run `.ralph/task_switch.sh`.

- Created main code commit `1a5945a` for the API startup boundary cleanup.
- Post-commit progress writes dirtied tracked `.ralph` files again, so I am making a small follow-up Ralph state commit before pushing.
- Next: push the branch, then run `.ralph/task_switch.sh`.
